clue.text: Arrange return of .musical to holding agency

parts.note: to arrange a meeting is to fix it

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the show's name is read from its end

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón

explanation.surface: A theatrical agency sets about bringing a hit show back.
explanation.walkthrough: Evita is a well-known stage musical; 'return of' reads it backwards as ATIVE. 'holding agency' sounds like a company but means a substance that holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixative is a substance such as glue or hair lacquer whose job is to hold things in place.

clue.text: Depart like immortal, old warriors

parts.note: the old army song says old soldiers never die, they simply slip from sight

explanation.definitionFit: To fade away is to vanish gradually, as the song says of old soldiers who never die.

clue.text: Scold an Athenian's wife.

definitions.meaning: the wife of Socrates, the Athenian philosopher

explanation.definitionFit: Socrates' wife was famed for a sharp tongue, so her name became a byword for a shrewish nag.

clue.text: Trunk springing from tangled roots

indicators.note: something tangled is twisted out of order, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A tree trunk rises from a mass of twisted roots.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the human body, without head or limbs, is the torso.

clue.text: A short -holiday 'could be nice with cover against sickness

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a holiday

indicators.note: could be says the letters might form something else when reordered

explanation.surface: A brief holiday would be pleasant if you had insurance against falling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaccine gives protection against a disease, a cover in the insurance sense.

clue.text: Shellfish extract

definitions.meaning: a small edible sea snail eaten with a pin
to prise it out with effort

explanation.definitionFit: The sea snail and the verb of prising out, as in getting a secret from someone, share one spelling.

clue.text: Money in cricket may be gold to a tax official

indicators.note: in places the money's letter inside the creature

parts.note: a cricket is one kind of insect
p is the abbreviation for penny or pence
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Cricket earnings may look like gold to a taxman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P inside INSECT to give INSPECT. The surface suggests the sport, but the cricket is the chirping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector of taxes is the official who examines tax returns.

clue.text: Honour for, sovereign Church body

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king
the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: A monarch confers an honour on a church assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the honours are the ace, king, queen, jack and ten; the jack is also called the knave.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack in cards is one of the high-ranking cards called honours in bridge.

clue.text: A screen for the viewer.

parts.note: suggests a television screen, but the viewer is the eye and the screen is its covering fold

explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin that closes over the eye shields it like a shutter.

clue.text: Get a severe test for taking notes into examination

indicators.note: into places the two notes within the examination word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
D and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: A student taking notes into an exam is in for a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful trial, and in history a trial by fire or water.

clue.text: Tear back about one to the res-: :taurant car

indicators.note: about means the turned word wraps round the letter for one
back means the word for tear is read from its end

parts.note: to tear is to rend
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone rushes back to the dining car on a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REND into DNER; 'about' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: On a train the dining car, where meals are served, is also called a diner.

clue.text: Shine in organization of court. case

indicators.note: organizing the letters puts them into a new order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A barrister shines in the way a court case is run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organization of' rearranges COURTCASE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To coruscate is to sparkle or flash brilliantly, used of light and of wit.

clue.text: Goddess who died in smash-hit opera

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for died within the rearranged letters
smashing the words breaks their letters into a new order

parts.note: d is the standard abbreviation for died in records and genealogies

explanation.surface: An opera about a goddess who dies becomes a smash hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smash' rearranges HITOPERA into APHROITE; 'in' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek deity of love and beauty, counterpart of the Roman Venus.

clue.text: Fragrant exudation from the: Matabele mimosa

indicators.note: from tells you to take the letters out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A scented gum oozes from an African mimosa tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and ointments.

clue.text: Tell value when article brought. in

indicators.note: the answer becomes the word for value only once the article is brought into it, so that word stands with the article taken back out

parts.note: to value something is to appraise it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone states a price once an item has been brought in for valuation.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: add A to the answer and you get APPRAISE, to value. So take A out of APPRAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to inform them of something.

clue.text: In which citations of the brave are presumably written

definitions.text: In which citations of the brave are presumably written

parts.words: In which citations of the brave are presumably written
parts.note: suggests medal citations for courage, but the brave are Native American warriors

explanation.definitionFit: A dense black drawing ink is named after a people, and the braves are warriors of the American plains.

clue.text: Offspring in a carrier

definitions.meaning: the young born to an animal at one birth, such as puppies
a curtained couch or stretcher on which a person is borne

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a brood of young animals and a stretcher or sedan for carrying people.

clue.text: Noted flier joins up with friend for an 'unlimited period

parts.note: noted read as given a note: E is a musical note set before the bird
a tern is a seabird, a flier
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A famous aviator teams up with a companion for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted flier' suggests a famous pilot; it is a bird with a musical note in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means forever, without end.

clue.text: Education deficient — through not being given lines?

definitions.meaning: read as without verses, as if no poetry was handed out

explanation.surface: A badly schooled pupil is one never set lines to write out.
explanation.definitionFit: Unversed means unskilled or ignorant in a subject, and read literally it means lacking verses.

clue.text: Fashion models not often available

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are shaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Top fashion models are rarely free to book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' rearranges MODELS. 'available' only fills out the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Seldom means rarely, on few occasions.

clue.text: Simply rely on me? No, just the opposite

indicators.note: the opposite order swaps the two words, sending the second to the front
in a down answer on means set above, so rely stacked on me puts rely first

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone says: just rely on me; no, the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rely on me' gives RELYME in a down answer; 'just the opposite' swaps the two words to put ME first.
explanation.definitionFit: Merely means only or just, nothing more.

clue.text: Build up rapidly with brigade leader heading drive forward

indicators.note: heading means the letter goes at the front of what follows
the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to urge on is to drive forward

explanation.surface: An army builds up fast with its brigade commander leading the advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes B from brigade; 'heading' puts it before URGE ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to grow or flourish quickly, like buds opening in spring.

clue.text: Alloy that is used in making wood

parts.note: brass is an alloy of copper and zinc
i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A metal alloy is used to make something wooden.
explanation.walkthrough: A wood is a golf club with a broad head; the brassie was an old one with a brass sole.
explanation.definitionFit: The brassie is a traditional golf club of the type known as woods, the modern two-wood.

clue.text: Stranger's drinking vessel

definitions.meaning: stranger is, more odd, rum being slang for odd

explanation.definitionFit: Rum means odd, so rummer is odder; a rummer is also a big drinking glass.

clue.text: Letter from Greece returned with bikini-top found in sunspot

indicators.note: returned means the Greek letter is sent back, read the other way

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the top half of a bikini is a bra

explanation.surface: A letter comes back from a Greek holiday with a bikini top found on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbra is the dark central region of a sunspot, ringed by the paler penumbra.

clue.text: Good French journalist, though spineless perhaps

parts.note: bon is French for good
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A fine French reporter turns out to be a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: Boned fish has had its backbone removed, hence spineless.
explanation.definitionFit: A boned fish or joint has its bones, including the spine, taken out.

clue.text: Soldiers are called in for further order

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of British army soldiers

indicators.note: in places the word for called inside the word are

parts.note: to call someone on the phone is to ring them, past tense rang

explanation.surface: Soldiers are summoned to receive fresh orders.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to put into a fresh sequence, ordering things a second time.

clue.text: Member of the Opposition showing dissent

definitions.meaning: one who stands against those in power

explanation.definitionFit: A rebel is a revolter against government, and as an adjective it means defiant.

clue.text: They make up part of the bill for service with-meals

definitions.text: They make up part of the bill for service with-meals

parts.words: They make up part of the bill for service with-meals
parts.note: reads like items on a restaurant bill, but the bill is a bird's beak, whose two jaws serve at mealtimes

explanation.definitionFit: Mandibles are the jaws, and in birds the upper and lower parts of the beak used for eating.

clue.text: Lightning strikers sometimes shot

definitions.meaning: streaks of lightning that strike the ground
fastenings on doors, or crossbow arrows, which are shot

explanation.definitionFit: The word means thunderbolts, and also door fasteners or crossbow missiles, which are shot.

clue.text: Heavenly sight delightful to Shepherd

parts.note: the weather saying that a glowing evening sky is a shepherd's delight

explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme runs 'at night, shepherd's delight', meaning a crimson evening sky promises fine weather.

clue.text: Set out to show a tricky manoeuvre indeed

annotationWithheld.why: Set out to show a tricky manoeuvre indeed (8): DEPLOYED is PLOY inside DEED, but 'indeed' must serve both as the container indicator 'in' and as the letters DEED, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Set out to show a tricky manoeuvre indeed
